_comment: ROUND-3 overnight pipeline config (run_training.py): the S-curve is mapped (DQN_REPORT §10, peak at S=5), so this run NARROWS to the winning neighborhood (S in {5,8}) and reinvests the budget in 8 training seeds for a low-variance winner + a reported seed std. Final eval auto-runs at the winning S (run_training reads dqn_sweep_results.json). Reward shape stays the round-1 bounded-stall winner. Commit this file with any change: a run is fully described by repo state.

lstm._signal: achieved = train on per-SEGMENT achieved-throughput series generated by gen_lstm_dataset.py under the current transport model (matches what the predictor is FED at inference); capacity = legacy DL_bitrate training
lstm._gen_args: 8 offsets because segment-level series are short (~30 samples per 300-frame episode at S=10) — more windows keep the sequence count healthy
lstm._sequence_length: 8 (was 20): at S=10 an episode only yields ~30 throughput samples, so seq_len 20 would leave the predictor cold for 2/3 of the episode

dqn_sweep._seeds: ROUND 3: EIGHT training seeds per config — round-2 showed a wide winner spread (seed 42->82 vs 43->62 QoE'), so this run averages 8 seeds and sweep.py now reports the per-config std of the selection metric. The winner level becomes trustworthy (mean ± std).
dqn_sweep._base_args: eval-seeds: every held-out eval averages 3 jitter seeds (kills the one-off-spike checkpoint problem). playback-rate-min 0.9 = research-backed imperceptible slowdown floor. reward-spec fixed to the round-1 winner shape.
dqn_sweep._axes: ROUND 3: narrowed to the round-2 winning neighborhood — S in {5,8} (the two best points), mu=4.3 (mu=2.0 was consistently worse), keep the lstm_pred ablation (the still-open question). 2 S x 1 mu x 2 lstm = 4 configs x 8 seeds = 32 trials (~2-3 h at jobs=2). The full S in {1,5,8,10,15,30} curve stays the record in DQN_REPORT §10.

final_eval._segment_frames: run_training.py evaluates at the WINNING S from dqn_sweep_results.json; this value is only the fallback when no sweep result exists.
